Hot tea and Apricots

By: Joy Summers | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Overnight she lost her voice, her vocal chord's would spasm and she would almost asphyxiate. Kim Ballantines story of loss and hope

Unique Selling Point:
Kim Ballantine and her husband Rob's story are a unique story of loss and hope combining faith, family and medical science.

Summary:
Kim Ballantine’s story of loss and hope.
On her 40th Birthday without warning, Kim Ballantine lost her voice. But not just her voice, and lost a means to communicate with her husband and her three young children. She also nearly lost her life several times as the condition spasmodic dysphonia impacted every aspect of the family life. The condition is neurological and most people never regain their ability to speak. For Kim it was also life threatening. When her vocal chords went into spasm, she was unable to breathe and several times she nearly asphyxiated. She had severe coughing spells that could be triggered by a sip of coffee ( everything through a straw). Mealtimes were a nightmare as she would splutter all over everybody. Her weight plummeted to around 43 kilograms. Doctors wanted to cut her vocal chords to save her life but she refused, holding onto her faith that one day she would talk again. But she would have to wait six and a half years. But Kim never gave up hope. Her strong faith was tested to its utmost as she battled through depression and the daily difficulties of her new life. She had to give up a successful career as an industrial psychologist in which she helped companies with their turnarounds. She had to learn how to sign and communicate with strangers who often mistook her as an idiot. Whistling became an integral part of the family life. Her husband Rob Ballantine, an ICU doctor saved her life many times but her inability to communicate put an enormous strain on their marriage. Nevertheless despite the hardships, they soldiered on, and if ever there was a book on how to be married in spite of difficulties this is it. Year after year she prayed and bargained with her God to bring back her speech, but nothing changed. Eventually to save her life she had a tracheostomy – a hole in the throat that enabled her to breath. She told the doctor that one day she would return for him to close up the hole.


Further information:
Then about 3 or 4 years into the condition – another shock. Kim discovered she had breast cancer. Her mother had died from it, so she went all in. Chemo and double mastectomy. But the chemo took its toll on her body, and she got sepsis. Not once, but three times, and she is probably only here because her husband Rob saved her life again and again, rushing her to hospital when she collapsed. The third time he set up an ICU tent in their bedroom and took off two weeks to treat her himself.
Then in year six one day, when was coming back from the hospital with her father and suddenly a small whisper. Kim’s voice was returning. No one could believe it, least of all her doctors. Rob had postulated that something else was driving the disease and it turned out that when the breast cancer had begun her body produced antibody proteins to fight the cancer. These proteins had in turn produced an autoimmune response that more than likely caused the condition. Little by little her voice returned, but the chemo and the cancer had weakened her so much she went into a deep depression. Her heart rate was through the roof and she couldn’t sleep at night. After all the medication she had been on, she resisted anti-depressants but she used them as a short term weapon to get through the final hurdles. This is a beautiful story of one family’s loss, hope and eventual triumph.

Hot Tea and Apricots FINAL SCRIPT Friday 28th June 2024
Audio
Kim Ballantine reading
There is a moment in life that creates a chasm, a great divide… the before and after where nothing is ever the same.

Voice over one
For Kim Ballantine, that moment was in a doctor's room. Almost overnight, Kim had lost her ability to speak

Up sound lift

Kim
The doctor told us that it was chronic and when we were standing in the lift about to go, this word bugged me, I don't have words and I tried to mouth to him- how long?

Voice over 2
Her husband Rob, with her at the time, and himself a doctor, understood what was meant when her condition was described as chronic.

Kim
And he just said to me Kimmie, chronic is forever. He has told you that you will never speak again and my whole world just involuted.

Voice over 3
Kim had been diagnosed with Spasmodic Dysphonia

Kim Ballantine
I lost my work, some people just ran, they didn't know what to do with what had happened to us. The children lost the mom they knew, and Rob definitively lost the wife he had fallen in love with. So the loss was extreme

Voice over four
Now she has told her story of loss and hope, and a family that navigated one life threatening moment after another.

Masa
It must have been a very dark space for you?
Kim
Absolutely. Just this wow! Inability to believe this is your life. I remember writing on a piece of paper, I will speak again. You don’t know how big my God is, or how determined I am. And one day I will have a story to tell.

FADE TO BLACK

Voice over five
In 2004 Kim had three children under ten, and a successful career as an industrial psychologist. Her husband Rob was a busy ICU physician. But everything changed on her 40th birthday when her vocal chords went into spasm.

Kim
And in a short period of time those spasms just ended up in G A GA GA, a very garbled voice if I tried to speak and then my vocal chords would close. I describe it as sucking against a balloon. I felt like I was drowning on dry land.

Voice over six
Within days, it was so bad, Rob had to urgently get her to hospital. Kim was unable to breathe.

Her eldest daughter Natalie, around ten at the time, recounts that her mother would frequently choke

Natalie Van Reenen
Everything is calm and normal and suddenly she would start coughing, her head would go back like this and gasping and gasping the whole time. I would jump up and hit her back and Heimliching hoping that would break it.

Voice over seven
Her brother Ryan Ballantine was only seven.

Ryan
You are a child you don’t know how to handle this and she is just steadily turning bluer and bluer.

Voice over eight
The treatment was Botox injected into her vocal chords

Kim
I had no idea that Botox was a neurotoxin that would paralyse my whole vocal complex, and that would last 6- 8 weeks, at any given time.
Masa
The doctors also wanted to cut your vocal chords?
Kim
Eventually the Botox wasn’t working. But if you cut those vocal chords you take away hope. And I just signed to him, you can’t take hope away from me. You can't take hope.

Voice over nine
The only way she could eat, was through a straw. Her weight plummeted to around 43 kilograms. Anything could set off her spasms.

Natalie Van Reenen
Suddenly out of nowhere my mom would spray whatever she was eating. Often she would stand up and the food was spilled across the table and it was jumping up and hitting
Ryan
And it's that violent arms up, everything goes.

Voice over 10
Kim called in a friend to teach them sign language. Her condition was getting worse

KIM
The period between the Botox was getting smaller and smaller. My relapses were more frequent. The trauma of it was just extreme.

Voice over 11
Two very difficult years passed and an almost perfect marriage grew fragile. Rob was so busy in ICU he didn't have time to master sign language.

Kim Ballantine
With every hand sign we were learning, The children and I got closer and closer. He and I moved further apart.

MASA
And you said, I know the stranger he is describing is me. He said I don't know how to say this any other way, you are no longer the woman I married.

Kim responds holding back tears…
Kim
It was so difficult looking at him, longing for a woman that short of a miracle was not going to come back.

Voice over 12
Rob the specialist physician was unable to fix his wife
Kim
He was looking at it like taking a Rubic’s cube and rotating every permutation. So I think in many ways I felt that medicine had failed him.

Voice over 13
A tracheostomy, a surgical opening in the wind pipe would bring some level of normality back to their lives The prospect of death from choking, was finally over.

LINK
And then a double whammy. Four years in with no voice Kim was diagnosed with breast cancer. They knew they were in for the fight of their lives

Voice over 14
Rob broke the news to her.

Rob
It was up to me to sit on the bed and say, hey babe, this is a tough one. This is breast cancer.

Kim
And I just signed to him and said this chose the wrong woman. It will not take me down.

Voice over 15
They treated the cancer aggressively with chemo and a double mastectomy. Kim was so weak she wanted to give up. But then something unexpected happened.

Kim
And I remember in April of 2009 writing, that I have an audible whisper and it sounds just like me. It almost feels like this massive miracle is happening in front of your eyes
Masa
And did you know what is bringing your voice back at that point.
Kim
No we didn't, we had no idea.

Voice over 16
Rob had always believed there was something else causing her voice loss. Then he and a few doctors, began to put the puzzle together

Rob
And the chemotherapy then, was when Kim’s voice came back
Masa
What was that like?
Rob
So that was when we started to see what this was all about. Any cancer can produce proteins that will be active in a different location in the body, and these proteins were affecting the nerves that were providing enervation to her vocal chords.

Voice over 16
In other words, her own body attacked her vocal complex when an immune response was triggered by the abnormal proteins from premalignant cells. The real cause, her breast cancer, was only discovered four and a half years later during treatment.

Rob
For years you have no communication and all of a sudden increasingly being able to speak! You know so much of our relationship that we had lost was accessible and available to us again!

Voice Over 17
But still Kim was not out of danger. The chemo had made her so weak that Sepsis nearly killed her three times. Twice Rob would save her life.

Kim
And I remember Rob saying you are so ill if you can't fight anymore it's ok you will be fine. You can let go. And he said can you do that and I just said no. And he said to me close your eyes -can you imagine your first grandchild? Can you imagine nibbling its toes, and sucking its ear because I know you would do that. Can you just smell this little one and he said Kim that is what you are living for and that night, just multiple times saying God I choose life, I choose life! I choose life!

Voice over 18
The third time, Rob set up an ICU in their bedroom and treated her at home.

Rob
So hugely privileged with her third episode of sepsis to be able to say- let's do this at home

Voice over 19
Kim now leads a full life as an executive and personal coach. She has been around for her first grandchildren, and is loving time with Rob, who has recently retired.

Natalie
There is a quote from Shawshank redemption. Hope is a good thing, maybe the best thing and no good thing ever dies

Up sound laugh and music

Rob
I have learned from Kim with such immense tenacity and resilience. Never give up hope. Irrespective of the loss. Look at the loss in its face but understand there is alway a hope beyond, and focus on doing the hope with the best application that you can.

THE END

Promo One.
Voice over
A rare condition took away Kim Ballantines voice for almost 6 years
Kim
My vocal chords would close. I describe it as sucking against a balloon. I felt like I was drowning on dry land.

Voice over
She lost her voice, her career, and she nearly lost her life. But that was not the end of her story.

PROMO TWO
Voice over
When Kim Ballantine lost her voice, her life as a mother, wife and businesswoman changed overnight

Kim
It was so difficult looking at him, longing for a woman that wasn't short of a miracle, going to come back.
Voice over
Now she recounts her story of loss, hope, faith and family





PROMO THREE
Voice over
When Kim Ballantine’s voice disappeared for almost six years, the doctors said she would never speak again.
Kim
I remember Rob that night saying to me you are so ill if you can't fight anymore, it's ok we will be fine. You can let go
Voice over
And no one was prepared for the strange medical twist in her story.

STRAPS
ROB BALLANTINE
KIM BALLANTINE
NATALIE VAN REENEN
RYAN BALLANTINE

Year after year she prayed and bargained with her God to bring back her speech, but nothing changed. Eventually to save her life she had a tracheostomy – a hole in the throat that enabled her to breath. She told the doctor that one day she would return for him to close up the hole.
metadata.Further information: Then about 3 or 4 years into the condition – another shock. Kim discovered she had breast cancer. Her mother had died from it, so she went all in. Chemo and double mastectomy. But the chemo took its toll on her body, and she got sepsis. Not once, but three times, and she is probably only here because her husband Rob saved her life again and again, rushing her to hospital when she collapsed. The third time he set up an ICU tent in their bedroom and took off two weeks to treat her himself. Then in year six one day, when was coming back from the hospital with her father and suddenly a small whisper. Kim’s voice was returning. No one could believe it, least of all her doctors. Rob had postulated that something else was driving the disease and it turned out that when the breast cancer had begun her body produced antibody proteins to fight the cancer. These proteins had in turn produced an autoimmune response that more than likely caused the condition. Little by little her voice returned, but the chemo and the cancer had weakened her so much she went into a deep depression. Her heart rate was through the roof and she couldn’t sleep at night. After all the medication she had been on, she resisted anti-depressants but she used them as a short term weapon to get through the final hurdles. This is a beautiful story of one family’s loss, hope and eventual triumph.
